headline: Y Combinator's Garry Tan spends up to $200K a year on AI agents' tokens for work and personal tasks
summary: Y Combinator CEO Garry Tan revealed he spends up to $200,000 annually on AI tokens, leveraging agents for extensive work projects, coding, and personal life management, including reading emails and therapy notes. He foresees personal AI agents becoming mainstr
details: Y Combinator CEO Garry Tan revealed on Walter Isaacson's podcast, "The Builders," that he spends between $100,000 and $200,000 annually on AI tokens. This significant expenditure fuels his use of AI agents for a wide range of professional and personal applications.

Tan utilizes AI agents for countless work projects and coding tasks, even sharing his set of 23 Claude Code skills, dubbed 'gstack,' on GitHub. He aims to demonstrate the capabilities of these agents to a broader audience.

Beyond professional use, his AI agent assists in managing his personal life. It has access to all his emails, Dropbox files, Apple Notes, and even therapy notes spanning 20 years, acting as a "Jiminy Cricket" that anticipates needs and offers proactive assistance.

As an early adopter and power user of OpenClaw, Tan emphasizes that AI agents should not be treated like traditional software. He cautions against prioritizing repeatability and safety to the extent that it sacrifices the "beautiful parts" of working with AI, which can be similar to human interaction.

Y Combinator itself employs an internal AI agent named "Stray Light" that possesses a distinct personality and a comprehensive "company brain." This agent holds the total context of every founder backed, all incoming emails, and applications.

Tan, a fervent technologist, believes that personal AI agents will eventually become mainstream. However, he identifies a major hurdle: the current high cost, acknowledging his own spending as a "crazy privilege" not accessible to everyone.

He also expresses concern about free, big-tech-controlled agents, drawing parallels to social media algorithms that users wish they didn't control. Tan envisions a future where personal AI agents are user-controlled and programmable, offering true autonomy.

headline: Apple forecasts biggest revenue quarter ever despite supply constraints
summary: Apple expects its December quarter to be its highest revenue in company history, even as it faces ongoing supply chain issues with the iPhone Duo.
details: During its fiscal Q4 2026 earnings call, Apple announced it expects the upcoming December quarter to be the best for revenue in the company's history. This optimistic forecast comes despite significant supply constraints impacting key products.

Specifically, Apple noted difficulties with the iPhone Duo, stating it's 'hard to predict' when these supply chain issues will improve. The company is navigating these challenges while still projecting record-breaking financial performance.
